title: One round trip per row: a page whose work grows with its list

source.says: the census's own model: one remote lookup per list row; logical data demand should not impose unnecessary serial or per-row round trips (H07). S33 is the overload a multiplied demand causes, not an N+1 incident. A dated primary source is still to be found, so this exhibit does not yet qualify under the ADR's rule and is shown as a miss pending its source

claim: none: the census marks H07 'specified but unproven' (batch only with equivalent authorization, consistency, limits and failure semantics; report unbatchable causes)

repro.how: a price per menu item read in the Server Component with `Promise.all(menu.map(..))`, one round trip each, counted at `/bench/queries`; the repair reads every price in one round trip

pleris.why: a query whose body maps a read over a list, `List.map(items, item => Menus.price(item.id))`, checks clean when its effect row declares the read; nothing batches it or refuses it
pleris.faithful: The same per-item read on the benchmark's store: `Menus.price` per item, inside a public query over the menu. The generality corpus accepts the same shape as a valid neighbour (examples/generality/undeclared_effect/complete-row.pw). A runtime count of the host's round trips is still to be added.
